text:
Dalien Brock was a Force-sensitive
Human male born of two Je'daii Masters, who reluctantly trained as a Je'daii Journeyer of the Je'daii Order with his sister, Lanoree, before fleeing after having killed Skott Yun, another Journeyer. After faking his death, he joined and led a sect of the Stargazers, a cabal of fanatics dedicated to finding a way to leave Tython system and to reach the stars of their ancestors by any means.

text: Deela jan Morolla was a Je'daii Master serving the Je'daii Order on Tython circa 32,920 BBY. She warned that not all Je'daii Journeyer would complete their Great Journey, as Tython and the morality of the Order posed a great many challenges to the youth. But Morolla also warned that Je'daii should accept these loses as life was not driven by absolutes, but by challenges. In 32,914 BBY, Morolla would be quoted as encouraging Je'daii to remember that the inhabitants of the system were brought to Tython, and that the world existed long before they arrived. The Master cautioned that Tython's age was deep, and that the Je'daii were merely passing through, and that their true home was the Force.
title: Deela jan Morolla — lead

text: Ironholgs was nickname given to an upgraded version of a Holgorian IM-220 maintenance droid associated with Je'daii Ranger Lanoree Brock. Ironholgs was responsible for basic onboard maintenance and security of Brock's ship; though it did not have arms. In addition to its basic protocols, Ironholgs was capable of remotely piloting the Peacemaker-class cruiser during missions. Brock also used it to record her journal. After their adventures on Sunspot, a damaged Ironholgs was in need of repair and Brock left him at Anil Kesh on Tython by a Je'daii Journeyer who specialized in mechanics.

text: Je'daii training was the action of teaching an apprentice the ways of the Force in the Je'daii Order on Tython. Force-sensitive beings were brought to Padawan Kesh from across the Tython system and trained as Je'daii initiates. If they passed the Padawan Trial, the younglings advanced to the next stage of their training as the Padawan of a Je'daii Master. Once a Padawan's training was complete, normally when the Padawan was in their teens, they were made Je'daii Journeyers and sent on their Great Journey: an odyssey across the surface of Tython to visit each of the nine Je'daii Temples. If the Journeyer survived, upon the successful completion of their Great Journey they were elevated to the rank of Je'daii Ranger. If a Je'daii Ranger had shown sufficient experience, wisdom, and understanding of the Force, they might be promoted to the rank of Je'daii Master, which was the highest rank a Je'daii could achieve other than a Je'daii Temple Master.
title: Je'daii training — lead

text: Kara was an obese Human female who lived on the planet Kalimahr in the Tython system during the reign of the Infinite Empire; although like all residents of the system, she was unaware of the Rakata and their Empire's existence in the greater galaxy. A former Je'daii, Kara had served the Je'daii Order on Tython long enough to come into the possession of a Force-imbued blade, but abandoned Tython to become a socialite in the city of Rhol Yan. Secretly, she and other wealthy individuals on Kalimahr served as the leadership of the Stargazers, funneling money to keep open hideouts and to pay for acolytes to move about in accordance to their master plan of leaving the isolated system and discovering the galaxy beyond.
title: Kara (Je'daii) — lead

text:
Knights of the Old Republic 0 was a supplemental comic to Dark Horse's Knights of the Old Republic comic series. It was included in the Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic/Rebellion flip-book.

The idea of such a flip-book was suggested by John Jackson Miller when the Knights of the Old Republic series was already in production. As a result, Brian Ching was distracted from drawing the main series, and Travel Foreman drew the fifth issue instead. Issue 0 was actually released after issue 1, and served as a prequel of sorts, but the issues were reordered chronologically for the trade paperback.

text: A Ranger star was a symbol worn by the members of the Je'daii Order that marked the rank of the Je'daii Ranger. The symbol was made in the form of a miniature metal star. Je'daii Rangers usually placed the star on their belts or other prominent places; they were recognized by such a star by the Padawans and the civilians among whom Rangers spent time on their assignments outside their homeworld of Tython. In order to blend in with the crowd and not give away their status, Je'daii Rangers hid their Ranger star.

text: Shall Mar was a Je'daii Master serving the Je'daii Order on Tython circa 28,915 BBY. He was known for having written the A Life in Balance, a book destined to be read by generations of Je'daii that would succeed him. The text was written between 28,930 and 28,918 BBY. In his text, Mar encouraged Je'daii to rely on their own innate talents and skills rather than calling on the Force for all their needs. While it could sustain a Je'daii, Mar postulated, it was but one tool in their arsenal. Additionally, in regard to Tython and the path of a Je'daii, Mar warned that they most know their limits and understand that not all hidden spaces should be sought out. The copy of [quoted words omitted] owned by Lanoree Brock's father was produced with great care.
title: Shall Mar — lead

text: The Shunned were a group of Force-sensitives, often former or failed Je'daii from the planet Tython, in the time more than seven centuries before the formation of the Galactic Republic during the reign of the Infinite Empire. The Je'daii order occasionally had individuals in whom the Force never settled and was not in balance in light or dark. They were never comfortable with the Force to the point that it actually [quoted words omitted] them. These individuals often felt a pull from outside the Tythan system. Often times this leads to their confinement on Bogan. For some this wasn't effective and those were [quoted words omitted] to head to the farthest reaches of the Tythan system and either go mad or die. The Stargazers were founded by one of the Shunned named Dalien Brock. The first example is a rich, large Kalimahr business woman named Kara, aged 70, whose mind was unreadable by the Je'daii Ranger Lanoree Brock sent to investigate. Lanoree assumed that Kara was a Je'daii but Kara denied saying that the Force had gone [quoted words omitted] in her.
title: Shunned — lead

text: Star Wars: The Old Republic, Threat of Peace is a series of webcomics that ties in to the Star Wars: The Old Republic massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) by LucasArts and BioWare. Written by Robert Chestney and illustrated by Alex Sanchez, the series was published in installments of three pages every other Friday through 2009 and early 2010 by Dark Horse Comics on StarWarsTheOldRepublic.com. The series was later reprinted in comic book form, and then collected in a trade paperback. Threat of Peace focuses on the Treaty of Coruscant and its aftermath, but as the series was released particularly early during the development of The Old Republic, the appearance of many elements and characters in the comics is radically different from the finalized versions that appear in The Old Republic.
